A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf v_1, \ldots, \mathbf v_n \in \R^n$.
Then the [[Definition:Volume|volume]] of the [[Definition:Simplex|simplex]] with vertices $\mathbf 0, \mathbf v_1, \ldots, \mathbf v_n$ is:
:$\dfrac {\size {\map \det {\mathbf v_1, \ldots, \mathbf v_n} } } {n!}$

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf v_1, \mathbf v_2 \in \R^2$.
Then the [[Definition:Area|area]] of the [[Definition:Triangle (Geometry)|triangle]] with vertices $\mathbf 0, \mathbf v_1, \mathbf v_2$ is:
:$\dfrac {\size {\map \det {\mathbf v_1, \mathbf v_2} } } 2$

derived.the parallelogram cut in half by a diago: the parallelepiped cut into n factorial congruent simplices
derived.the area formula: the volume formula, recovering the triangle case at n = 2

object_map.reformulation: Replace the two-dimensional halving by the decomposition of a cube into n factorial ordered regions.

validity_conditions: The parallelepiped spanned by the vectors has volume the absolute determinant, which is the base case the argument builds on.
That parallelepiped decomposes into n factorial simplices, one for each ordering of the coordinates, all congruent by permutation of coordinates.
The vectors must be linearly independent for the simplex to be nondegenerate; otherwise both sides vanish and the statement is trivially true.
proof_plan: The [[Definition:Parallelepiped|parallelepiped]] spanned by $\mathbf v_1, \ldots, \mathbf v_n$ has volume $\size {\map \det {\mathbf v_1, \ldots, \mathbf v_n} }$.

Decompose the unit cube $\closedint 0 1^n$ into the $n!$ regions:
:$\set {x: x_{\map \sigma 1} \ge x_{\map \sigma 2} \ge \cdots \ge x_{\map \sigma n} }$
for $\sigma \in S_n$, which overlap only on sets of measure zero.

These regions are congruent under permutation of coordinates.
Hence each has volume $\dfrac 1 {n!}$; one of them is the standard simplex $\set {1 \ge x_1 \ge \cdots \ge x_n \ge 0}$, which is linearly equivalent to $\map {\operatorname {conv} } {\mathbf 0, e_1, \ldots, e_n}$ by a map of determinant $\pm 1$.
